Hit score of a geographic profile

Source: R/rtm.R
hitscr.Rd

A geographic profile ranks the cells of a search area; searched from the highest score down, the hit score is the share of the area searched before the offender's home is reached (Rossmo 2000), the smaller the better. Cells scored the same as the home cell are counted both ways: hit searches them after the home, hitt before it.

Usage

hitscr(s, home)

Arguments

s

The scores of the cells: finite numbers, higher searched first (a profile from jtsurf(), say).

home

The cells holding the home: cell numbers from 1 to length(s), one or several (several offenders, or candidate homes).

Value

A data frame with one row per home: home, above (the cells scored higher), ties (the cells scored the same, the home included), rank (above + 1), and the hit scores in per cent, hit (100 * above / length(s)) and hitt (100 * (above + ties) / length(s)).

References

Rossmo, D. K. (2000). Geographic Profiling. CRC Press.

Examples

hitscr(c(0.9, 0.5, 0.7, 0.5, 0.1), home = 2)
#>   home above ties rank hit hitt
#> 1    2     2    2    3  40   80
